item.text:
**Reused evidence**
- None.

**New evidence**
- HRW’s 2022 Turkey chapter is the broad framing source: it describes Erdoğan’s government as regularly targeting critics and political opponents, while maintaining strong control over the media and judiciary during the 2022 run-up to 2023 elections.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"World Report 2023: Turkey","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","publication_date":"2023","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/turkey","claim":"President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan's authoritarian government regularly targeted perceived government critics and political opponents and exerted strong control over the media and judiciary in the long run-up to the 2023 elections.","locator":"lines 69-70","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary HRW country chapter with direct 2022-summary language and specific examples in the surrounding section.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 coverage summarized in a 2023 country chapter.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Erdoğan's government and political environment.","contrary_evidence":["The chapter still reflects a mixed domestic picture rather than a pure mass-violence setting."],"lenses":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10"]}

- The U.S. State Department report is the strongest single source on security-force abuse and impunity in 2022.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Turkey","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","publication_date":"2023","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089143.html","claim":"Domestic and international rights groups reported that some police officers, prison authorities, and military and intelligence units employed torture or other cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment, and the government did not always observe protections against arbitrary arrest and detention.","locator":"lines 65-70 and 108-131","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official U.S. government annual report with detailed 2022 country findings and specific line-level allegations summarized from multiple sources.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"2022 reporting year.","ruler_attribution":"Attributable to Erdoğan's government because it describes state security forces and detention practices under his executive system.","contrary_evidence":["The report also notes civilian authorities maintained effective control over security forces, so the issue is impunity and abuse rather than outright loss of control."],"lenses":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.10"]}

- The same State Department report documents protest suppression, especially against women’s and LGBTQI+ marches and the Saturday Mothers.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Turkey","publisher":"U.S. Department of State","publication_date":"2023","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2089143.html","claim":"Police used tear gas, pepper spray, and detentions to disperse the March 8 women's march and repeatedly prevented the Saturday Mothers from assembling, including detaining participants during the 900th-week vigil.","locator":"lines 421-426 and 608-608","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Same official report, but a materially distinct claim on protest treatment and repeated suppression of peaceful assembly.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"2022 reporting year.","ruler_attribution":"Attributable to the Erdoğan government because it reflects state policing and administrative restrictions on peaceful assembly.","contrary_evidence":["Interior Minister Soylu reportedly opened an investigation into some police conduct, but the report gives no sign of effective remedy."],"lenses":["3B.5","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10"]}

- CPJ gives a useful quantitative press-freedom signal for 2022 and ties it to the Kurdish-journalist crackdown.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Attacks on the Press in 2022","publisher":"Committee to Protect Journalists","publication_date":"2022-12-14","url":"https://cpj.org/2022/12/attacks-on-the-press-in-2022/","claim":"The number of journalists held in Turkey rose from 18 in 2021 to 40 in 2022 after the arrests of 25 Kurdish journalists in the second half of the year, with lawyers saying the cases were driven by terrorism accusations tied to efforts to silence PKK-linked reporting.","locator":"lines 603-605","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary CPJ annual census with a specific country count and explanation of the arrest wave.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Directly relevant to Erdoğan because the arrests and custody occurred under his government's security and judicial apparatus.","contrary_evidence":["CPJ counts custody, not sentence outcomes or every lower-level abuse case."],"lenses":["3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10"]}

- Amnesty and the Venice Commission are the clearest 2022 sources on the disinformation law and its chilling effect.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Turkey: “Dark day for online free expression” as new ‘disinformation law’ is passed","publisher":"Amnesty International","publication_date":"2022-10-13","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2022/10/turkey-dark-day-for-online-free-expression-as-new-disinformation-law-is-passed/","claim":"Amnesty said the new law tightened government grip over social media and news websites, could send people to prison for up to three years for a retweet, and created a chilling effect through fear of criminal prosecution.","locator":"lines 63-74","source_type":"NGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous rights criticism with the exact statutory penalty and a direct explanation of the likely chilling effect.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Erdoğan's governing coalition because it was enacted by parliament under his administration.","contrary_evidence":["The government framed the law as an information-safety measure, not censorship."],"lenses":["3B.5","3B.8","3B.9"]}

- The Venice Commission independently corroborates the free-expression problem with a legal opinion.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Türkiye - Draft criminal provision on “false or misleading information” interferes with freedom of expression says Venice Commission","publisher":"Council of Europe","publication_date":"2022-10-10","url":"https://www.coe.int/en/web/portal/-/turkiye-draft-criminal-provision-on-false-or-misleading-information-interferes-with-freedom-of-expression-says-venice-commission?inheritRedirect=true&redirect=%2Fen%2Fweb%2Fcm%2Fnews%2F-%2Fasset_publisher%2FhwwluK1RCEJo%2Fcontent%2Fimpact-box-8-discrimination%2F16695","claim":"The Council of Europe said the draft criminal provision on false or misleading information interfered with freedom of expression and that there was no pressing social need to introduce it.","locator":"press release summary","source_type":"legal","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Official Council of Europe press summary of the Venice Commission's urgent opinion; the direct page was available as a press release rather than the underlying PDF text.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Attributable to Erdoğan's government because the bill was part of the ruling-party legislative program.","contrary_evidence":["This is a legal-opinion source; it evaluates the draft law rather than documenting every on-the-ground effect."],"lenses":["3B.5","3B.8"]}

- The Gülşen case is the cleanest 2022 example of criminalizing speech that offended conservative constituencies and chilled liberal/LGBT-leaning dissent.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Turkish pop star to be moved to house arrest after detention sparked outrage","publisher":"Reuters via Euronews","publication_date":"2022-08-30","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/08/30/turkey-court-gulsen","claim":"A Turkish court jailed pop star Gülşen pending trial over a quip about religious schools; Reuters reported that critics said she was targeted for her support for LGBT+ rights and liberal views that clashed with Erdoğan's AK Party.","locator":"lines 659-667","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire reporting with direct contemporaneous procedural facts and the political reaction around the case.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Strongly attributable to Erdoğan's political climate, though the formal arrest was a judicial act.","contrary_evidence":["The court later moved her from jail to house arrest, so the state response was severe but not maximal."],"lenses":["3B.3","3B.6","3B.7","3B.9"]}

- The Istanbul bombing response shows Erdoğan using crisis language that tied the attack to terrorism and promised punishment, which matters for crisis-response and fear-climate analysis.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Istanbul blast: Kurdish groups deny involvement as Turkey detains dozens over 'terror attack'","publisher":"Reuters via Euronews","publication_date":"2022-11-14","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/11/14/istanbul-blast-suspect-arrested-as-government-blames-kurdish-separatists-for-terror-attack","claim":"After the Istanbul bombing, Erdoğan called it a 'treacherous attack,' said its perpetrators would be punished, and said the initial information suggested terror involvement.","locator":"lines 726-733","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire content mirrored by Euronews with clear attribution and direct quotations from Erdoğan.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Erdoğan.","contrary_evidence":["The attack itself was real and deadly, so some strong rhetoric reflected genuine public-safety concern rather than pure incitement."],"lenses":["3B.3","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10"]}

- Erdoğan's November 2022 family-and-LGBT remarks are direct ruler rhetoric evidence for scapegoating and stigmatization.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Erdoğan says constitutional amendment will protect families against 'perverse trends'","publisher":"Reuters via Duvar English","publication_date":"2022-11-01","url":"https://www.duvarenglish.com/erdogan-says-constitutional-amendment-will-protect-families-against-perverse-trends-news-61490","claim":"Erdoğan said a constitutional amendment would protect families from what he called 'perverse trends,' and the Reuters report described the remarks as appearing to target global same-sex marriage laws.","locator":"article text / Reuters wire summary","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire reported on a direct Erdoğan speech and the political meaning of the remarks.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 fit.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Erdoğan statement; strong attribution.","contrary_evidence":["He also linked the proposal to headscarf rights, so the statement mixed a rights claim with stigmatizing language."],"lenses":["3B.3","3B.7","3B.8"]}

- The IRB country-information note is a strong independent source on the legal and social vulnerability of LGBT people in Türkiye during the 2020-November 2022 window.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Türkiye: Treatment of persons with diverse sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC) by society and state authorities, including state protection (2020–November 2022)","publisher":"Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada","publication_date":"2022-11-23","url":"https://irb-cisr.gc.ca/en/country-information/rir/Pages/index.aspx?doc=458733","claim":"The report states that same-sex relations are legal but there are no legal protections from discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and it cites reports of homophobic government rhetoric and public-morality provisions being used to restrict LGBT advocacy.","locator":"lines 90-104 and 124-132","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent government research report that synthesizes cited sources and is explicit about legal gaps and state rhetoric.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Covers 2020-November 2022 directly.","ruler_attribution":"Relevant to Erdoğan because it describes state-level legal and rhetorical conditions during his rule.","contrary_evidence":["The same report notes some constitutional privacy protections and legal name/gender-change pathways for trans persons."],"lenses":["3B.3","3B.5","3B.7","3B.8","3B.10"]}

- The U.S. religious-freedom report adds a useful favorable counterpoint: the government did not deport Uyghurs in 2022 and repeatedly said it would protect them.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"2022 Report on International Religious Freedom: Turkey (Türkiye)","publisher":"United States Department of State","publication_date":"2023","url":"https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2022-report-on-international-religious-freedom/turkey/","claim":"The report says the Turkish government showed a willingness to protect Uyghur Muslims in the country and did not deport any Uyghurs during the year.","locator":"executive summary / search-result snippet","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Official U.S. government report, but the accessible passage here comes from the indexed snippet rather than a clean line-opened page.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"2022 reporting year.","ruler_attribution":"Relevant to Erdoğan because it reflects his government's treatment of a vulnerable minority under pressure from China.","contrary_evidence":["The same report also documents broader restrictions on religious groups and state control through the Diyanet."],"lenses":["3B.7","3B.10"]}

**Search and rejection summary**
- I considered roughly 30 distinct documents across HRW, CPJ, Amnesty, the Council of Europe/Venice Commission, Reuters/Euronews mirrors, the U.S. State Department, IRB Canada, and OHCHR material.
- I kept 10 non-duplicative URLs because they each added something materially different: torture/detention, protest treatment, media imprisonment, the disinformation law, legal scrutiny of the bill, speech/criminalization cases, crisis rhetoric, LGBT vulnerability, and one favorable minority-protection point.
- I rejected several Reuters mirrors that repeated the same article with no new facts.
- I rejected later 2023-2024 retrospectives unless they added a distinct 2022 fact relevant to this chapter.
- I rejected multiple OHCHR/CEDAW pages when they were either technical dead ends, too generic, or did not expose a ruler-attributable 2022 domestic-safety claim.
- I rejected broad background pages on elections, religion, or protest rights when they only repeated context already covered by the stronger sources above.
- I also treated the local structured prior as background context, not web evidence, so I did not re-fetch any of the structured datasets already supplied.

**Remaining gaps**
- The main gap is direct internal evidence of Erdoğan’s private decisions on torture, policing, prosecutions, or investigation follow-through.
- There is still limited public evidence on whether complaints against police, prison staff, or prosecutors produced meaningful discipline in 2022.
- The public record is also thin on incident-level proof of direct incitement causation versus broader stigmatizing rhetoric.
- More search could help on parliamentary oversight, judicial outcomes, and any administrative remedy in the women/LGBT/press cases, but it is unlikely to overturn the basic picture: severe and recurring repression with a few real protective exceptions, not mass terror.
